candidate: RA2 VM (ra2-games/ra2, live at ra2.games): runs the original x86 RA2 game.exe 1.006 and YR gamemd.exe 1.001 in the browser on v86, with custom firmware, a PE loader and HLE Win32/DirectX shims
summary: VERIFIED: The project exists and is public. It is GPL-3.0-or-later, about 38k lines of TypeScript, and its README calls it Alpha. It runs the unmodified RA2 1.006 and YR 1.001 executables inside v86 without booting Windows. The DirectDraw, DirectSound, Winsock/IPX, OLE and user32 calls are reimplemented in TypeScript, and the game's own 16-bit RGB565 software-rendered frame goes to a WebGL2 canvas. It already has: YR support, skirmish vs the original AI, native save/load, multiplayer over a WebSocket relay that emulates an IPX LAN, custom .yrm/.mpr map packages, top-level INI/MIX mod overrides (the 共和国之辉 mod is tested), Bink FMV through the original binkw32.dll, a GPU upscaler chain (FSR1/RCAS, ScaleFX, Anime4K CNN/GAN, and ONNX/WebGPU SR models in dev builds only) and a single-pass ReShade-style post-process hook. I cloned it and ran `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm run check` on the M5 Mac: 128 test files and 918 tests passed, and the production build succeeded. CORRECTION TO THE TASK BRIEF: HN item 45991853 ('Red Alert 2 in web browser', 497 points, 2025-11-20) links to chronodivide.com, a reimplementation. It is not RA2 VM. I found no HN thread for ra2.games. For this remaster the project is the fastest, most faithful route to Step 1, because the original game logic runs unchanged. Step 2 (real HD) is only partly possible today: every current enhancement works on the finished 2D frame. Genuine HD sprites, meshes, water and weather would need new guest-code hooks or reads of guest memory at game-specific addresses, which is a large reverse-engineering job. The authors document that plan but have only done a passthrough experiment.
license_evidence: VERIFIED: LICENSE holds the full GPLv3 text. package.json has "license": "GPL-3.0-or-later". README says 'Original project code is GPL-3.0-or-later'. The GitHub API reports spdx GPL-3.0. docs/THIRD_PARTY.md: v86 (BSD-2-Clause per https://github.com/copy/v86), React, 7z-wasm, fflate and onnxruntime-web keep their own licenses. Anime4K and SweetFX shaders and the AMD FSR1 and ScaleFX ports keep their MIT headers. The launcher background image has an unclear license. Game files are excluded. The optional SR model weights are NOT bundled: UltraSharpV2 and AnimeSharpV2 are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, APISR is GPL-3.0, NomosUni is CC BY 4.0 (docs/AI_UPSCALING.md). What this means for us (INFERENCE): a fork must stay GPL-3.0 and be distributed with source, and the non-commercial SR weights cannot ship in a public build.
provenance: Original work. It is not derived from Chrono Divide. The team is led by Junlin Liu (@NoCLin) with contributors listed from academia, and a lot of the code was written by an AI coding agent. The public repo receives squashed snapshots of an internal 'dev' branch.
provenance_evidence: VERIFIED: the repo was created 2026-09-12 under a new org, ra2-games ('Red Alert Games', blog ra2.games, one public repo). The first commits are 'init' and 'init OSS release', authored by 'agent <agent@anonymous.local>'. AGENTS.md (with CLAUDE.md symlinked to it) says 'Internal work uses dev, which is not pushed to GitHub'. CONTRIBUTORS.md lists Junlin Liu* (@NoCLin), Yuyuan Li (links to an hdu.edu.cn faculty page), Lin Zhao, Jiayuan Fang and Yifan Xu. The architecture is fundamentally different from Chrono Divide: it emulates the x86 binary rather than reimplementing the engine. The code says spawner work was 'independently written' and that CnCNet yrpp-spawner GPL code was 'not copied' (src/games/yr/spawnerProbe.ts). Game addresses come from the team's own disassembly (scripts/reverse/ra2Dis.mts and related scripts), with the evidence written up in the docs. Related but separate projects: BottleShip (https://github.com/jenissimo/bottleship, Apache-2.0, a v86 fork plus DirectDraw/D3D3-9 to WebGPU; its compatibility doc lists Tiberian Sun as 'playable' and RA2 is not listed) and vga-ddraw for v86 (https://github.com/copy/v86/discussions/1591, RA95 demo and StarCraft).
tech_stack: TypeScript 5.9, React 19, Vite 6, pnpm 11.24 (auto-switched from the installed 11.5.2), Vitest 4, Playwright 1.60. v86 0.5.441 (x86-to-wasm JIT) runs in a Web Worker, with a main-thread fallback. Custom 16-bit boot firmware is built with nasm (src/vm86/boot.asm and boot.bin). HLE shims live in src/vm86/shim: kernel32, user32, gdi32, DirectDraw, DirectSound, DirectPlay, ole32, winmm and Winsock. WebGL2 presenter; WebAudio AudioWorklet (pcmStreamWorklet); IndexedDB for resources and saves; 7z-wasm, fflate, LZMA and NSIS for importing installers and archives; onnxruntime-web 1.29 with WebGPU in dev builds only. A separate Node WebSocket relay package lives in packages/relay and ships with a Docker compose file. 640 MB guest RAM per game (src/games/catalog.ts).
renderer_architecture:
VERIFIED from code:
(1) The game keeps its own software renderer. The shim creates COM objects for IDirectDraw, IDirectDrawSurface, Clipper and Palette in guest memory (src/vm86/shim/directx.ts). GetCaps reports software blit, colour-key and palette capabilities only, with no 3D or overlay, so the game picks its CPU blitters.
(2) SetDisplayMode accepts 8 or 16 bpp at 320x200 up to 2560x1600. RA2/YR use 16-bit RGB565, not 8-bit. SHP, VXL and TMP assets are palettized, and the game's own x86 code decodes them into the RGB565 back buffer inside the emulated CPU. The browser only ever sees final pixels.
(3) Lock is a guest-side stub that copies a cached DDSURFACEDESC. Unlock, Blt and Flip are hypercalls into the host that mark surfaces dirty. stateGraphics.emitFrame() sends a VmFrame to the presenter: width, height, rgb565 or rgba or 8-bit indices plus palette, and a separate cursor bitmap (src/vm86/win32.ts:102).
(4) Frames go as exclusive buffers from the Worker to src/graphics/framePresenter.ts (newest frame wins) and on to src/ui/pages/game/vmFrameRenderer.ts. That renderer is WebGL2 with a Canvas2D fallback, uploads RGB565 as an integer texture, and fits the canvas at integer scales.
(5) Optional stages: Bicubic, FSR 1.0 EASU with RCAS (fsrUpscale.ts), ScaleFX 3x (scalefxUpscale.ts), Anime4K CNN-S or GAN-M 2x in GLSL (aiUpscale.ts), and in dev builds ONNX models on WebGPU (UltraSharpV2 Lite 4x, NomosUni SPAN 2x, AnimeSharpV2, APISR) capped at 800x600 input (experiments/modelProbe.ts).
(6) FramePostProcess/ColorPostProcess (src/graphics/framePostProcess.ts) runs one GLSL pass after the final colour and before the cursor. The production 'ReShade' menu offers ports of SweetFX Vibrance and LumaSharpen (src/graphics/reshadePreset.ts). An experimental LaserBlit FX-to-GLSL path (src/graphics/experimental/reshadeLaser.ts) has only been verified in passthrough mode.
There is no per-object lighting, depth or scene graph on the host side. Lighting is whatever the original engine bakes into the frame. Resolution presets go up to 1920x1080 (src/games/resolution.ts), set by patching RA2.INI/RA2MD.INI in an in-memory overlay.
activity: VERIFIED via GitHub API on 2026-09-27: 238 stars, 33 forks, 1 watcher, 0 open issues (1 closed: macOS saves, fixed), 3 PRs (#2 merged, #3 closed on 2026-09-27). The public repo was created 2026-09-12, so it is about 2 weeks old. Last push was 2026-09-21. There are 12 commits on main, all snapshot or squash releases (the internal dev branch is private). GitHub contributors: Yohoa (4), NoCLin (2), plus 'agent' commits. The org has no releases or tags. build_result: SUCCESS (asset-free). On macOS with Node v26.0.0 in scratchpad/repos/ra2vm__ra2-games__ra2: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` took about 1 s (112 packages; pnpm switched itself to v11.24.0). `pnpm run check` took about 17 s wall time: typecheck OK, then Vitest with 128 test files and 918 tests passed (including synthetic-PE tests that run real v86 x86 code), then the Vite production build succeeded (v86.wasm 2.1 MB, 7zz.wasm 1.65 MB, vmWorker 743 kB, page chunk 871 kB). `pnpm run dev` served HTTPS 200 on 127.0.0.1:15195. I did NOT run the actual game, for two reasons. (a) There are no RA2/YR files on this machine. (b) Opening the page makes src/main.ts call preloadThirdPartyFiles(), which automatically downloads EA's game.exe and gamemd.exe from https://oldgame.store (src/games/manifest.ts). That is copyrighted binaries from an unofficial host, so I stopped the dev server without loading the page in a browser. Real-game performance and fidelity are therefore UNMEASURED by me.
feature_completeness:
Because the original executables run, game rules are inherently the same as the original. That is an INFERENCE unless marked as tested.
- Skirmish vs AI (original easy/medium/brutal AI): VERIFIED in code and tests (tests/real-game/ra2/shortGame, skirmishSlots, battleStartup; the 'start-page=battle' hook).
- YR content: VERIFIED (gamemd.exe 1.001 profile, boot, startup-page, save/load and spawner-probe tests).
- Allied and Soviet campaigns: PARTIAL. The engine supports them and Maps01/02.mix are optional in the manifest. There is campaign-menu compatibility code (src/vm86/shim/state.ts campaignMenu, user32Windowing repairHiddenCampaignListBorder). But no campaign regression tests exist, and the README says short regressions 'do not establish compatibility with every campaign'. For YR campaign saves the docs say it 'retains its previous campaign policy until separately validated'.
- Online/LAN multiplayer: VERIFIED. Native IPX datagrams go over a WebSocket relay you host yourself, up to 8 in-game players and 20 relay members per room. Only short 2-client matches are tested. No reconnect or resume, no auth, no desync CRC acceptance, no public lobby. INFERENCE: no interop with CnCNet.
- All units, buildings and superweapons, naval units and water, bridges, garrisoning, veterancy, Chronosphere/Iron Curtain, fog and shroud: INFERENCE, faithful because it is the original code. None is individually tested.
- Custom maps: VERIFIED for .yrm and .mpr mounted from archives (src/adapter/customMapPackage.ts). .csf is stored but not mounted. Loose .map files are not handled by that dialog.
- Sound, EVA and music: VERIFIED. DirectSound is mapped to a WebAudio worklet (src/adapter/audio.ts), and Theme.mix/thememd.mix are optional.
- FMV: VERIFIED. The original BINKW32.DLL is loaded as a guest DLL (src/vm86/shim/stateGuestDll.ts), with sparse loading of movies mix files and a startup-movie skip.
- Save/load: VERIFIED. Native OLE IPersistStream serialization plus IndexedDB, with real-game cold-load regressions for RA2 and YR skirmish.
- Replays: NOT AVAILABLE. INFERENCE: the original RA2/YR has no replay system, and the project adds none.
- INI modding: VERIFIED for top-level rules.ini/art.ini/ai.ini and expand/ecache MIX overrides in RA2 (manifest.ts), and the 共和国之辉 mod test (tests/real-game/ra2/gonghui.test.ts). Ares, Phobos and Syringe are NOT supported (no grep hits; only a probe for the spawner entry point).
- Map editor: none. FinalAlert2/FinalSun is a native Windows tool, open-sourced by EA under GPL-3.0 (https://github.com/electronicarts/CNC_TS_and_RA2_Mission_Editor); INFERENCE: maps made there could be imported.
- Performance at high resolution: presets go up to 1920x1080 (the shim allows 2560x1600). All rendering happens in the single emulated CPU core, so cost grows with pixel count. INFERENCE from the AI_UPSCALING.md advice to 'Start with 800×600 game resolution' and GPU-upscale. The project ships a 20 s performance-diagnostics recorder (docs/GAME_PERFORMANCE.md) but publishes no FPS numbers. Other features: mobile touch controls, and iOS Safari-vs-Chrome comparison reports.
asset_requirements:
VERIFIED from src/games/manifest.ts. The user imports a folder or archive (zip, 7z, rar, or an NSIS installer).
- RA2 required: ra2.mix, language.mix, Binkw32.dll, Blowfish.dll.
- RA2 optional: Maps01/02.mix (campaigns), movies01/02.mix, Theme.mix, Multi.mix, Taunts/, and mod overrides.
- YR required: ra2md.mix, langmd.mix, BINKW32.DLL, Blowfish.dll.
- YR optional: expandmd01.mix, MAPSMD03.MIX, movmd03.mix, thememd.mix, MULTIMD.MIX.
The executables are NOT taken from the user's copy. They are exact-hash binaries (RA2 game.exe sha256 06f99496..., YR gamemd.exe sha256 7b8a0685...) fetched from https://oldgame.store/game.exe and /gamemd.exe on every page load (src/main.ts, src/adapter/thirdPartyFiles.ts). Every patch and hook checks that hash, so a different exe (for example Steam or EA App builds, if their bytes differ; unverified) would be rejected by the version-specific hooks. src/games/downloadCatalog.ts also links full-game downloads on unofficial sites (uc129.com, jb51.net, an archive.org XWIS installer). For our fork: source assets from a legally owned copy (for example the Steam 'Command & Conquer Red Alert 2 and Yuri's Revenge', app 2229850) and check whether its executables match the registered hashes. If not, re-verify every address.
hd_extensibility:
Layered options, from cheapest to deepest. The files named are where the work would go.

L0, available now: final-frame post-processing. src/graphics/framePostProcess.ts (ColorPostProcess) and src/ui/pages/game/vmFrameRenderer.ts (setPostProcess, setUpscaleMode) host GLSL passes. The FSR, ScaleFX, Anime4K and ONNX SR upscalers already work (aiUpscale.ts, fsrUpscale.ts, scalefxUpscale.ts, experiments/modelProbe.ts), plus SweetFX colour and sharpening (src/graphics/reshadePreset.ts). Easy wins: render at 800x600 or 960x540 and upscale 2–4x with a tuned model, add LUT colour grading, bloom and a sidebar mask. The sidebar sits at a fixed position, so masking it is inferred to be simple. Limit: no depth or object information, and effects also hit the UI (the docs admit the effects 'cover the whole final color frame, including the native sidebar').

L1: read helper buffers straight from guest RAM. v86 memory is a WASM ArrayBuffer that the host can read cheaply. GameRuntimeHooks (src/games/runtimeHooks.ts) already has a read-only memory reader pattern (src/games/yr/performance.ts reads counter 0xa8ed84 after checking the exe hash and instruction signatures). The same pattern can export YR's Z-buffer, A-buffer, shroud, tactical viewport rect and map-cell water/tile data each frame, using addresses from YRpp (https://github.com/Phobos-developers/YRpp, which targets YR 1.001 and has no license file). These become WebGL textures for depth-aware effects: modern water shading masked to water cells, rain and snow occluded by buildings, fog, AO-like darkening, and lights on explosions. docs/RESHADE_ADAPTATION.md describes exactly this bridge. It notes the Toumao (头猫) ReShade plugin uses the TOPMASK, LIGHT, ZBUFFER, SHROUD and WATER textures, but that none are exported yet ('Final frames alone cannot reproduce plugin water, occlusion, or layered high-resolution drawing').

L2: capture the game's draw calls. One-shot x86 trampolines already exist (src/games/shared/startupTrampoline.ts, src/games/shared/battleStartup.ts, src/games/yr/spawnerProbe.ts, each with hash and signature checks). Extending them to hook the SHP draw (YRpp CC_Draw_Shape), voxel draw, iso-tile draw and anim draw functions, and writing records into a guest-side ring buffer, avoids a hypercall per draw. The project already cut 'tens of thousands of VM/JS round trips per battlefield frame' (directx.ts:138), which shows hypercalls are the bottleneck. The host then draws HD replacements at 2–4x in WebGL2/WebGPU: AI-upscaled or re-painted PNG sprite sequences, and voxel-to-mesh (render the VXL or a new 3D mesh with PBR under a fixed isometric camera). It composites them over the upscaled original, keeping z-order, team colours, palette tint and shadows. This matches the Toumao plugin's native hooks (AnimClass_Draw_SetTexture, TechnoClass_RenderVxl_ReplaceMesh, GScreenClass_Update_TransferBuffer), as listed in RESHADE_ADAPTATION.md. Particles, impact and explosion effects, and modern water would live here too.

L3: host-side renderer. The original exe stays the simulation, and a new WebGPU 2.5D renderer draws everything from game state read out of guest memory (object lists, positions, facings, frames) or captured draw calls. The game's own blits could possibly be suppressed to save CPU. This is the C&C Remastered pattern and gives full 2026-level visuals while keeping 100% original logic. INFERENCE: feasible for YR, where YRpp documents the data structures. It is much harder for RA2 1.006, which has no comparable reverse-engineering database, and the docs say the two engines 'remain separate'.

Also: same-resolution MIX asset replacement already works (mod MIXes load). But because the engine draws at fixed pixel sizes, higher-resolution SHPs would appear physically larger rather than sharper. Raising ScreenWidth/Height only shows more of the map. Running Ares or Phobos inside the VM would need a Syringe-style hook installer in the PE loader (src/vm86/shim/stateGuestDll.ts already loads guest DLLs and runs DllMain) plus much wider Win32 and CRT coverage, since 'unimplemented calls must not default to success'. That is unproven work.

Native-Windows comparison (VERIFIED sources): gamemd.exe 1.001 can run with:
- Ares 3.0p1, which needs YR 1.001 (https://ares-developers.github.io/Ares-docs/notes.html). Its repo has no SPDX license.
- Phobos (GPL-3.0, 458 stars, pushed 2026-09-26, currently asking for maintainers; https://github.com/Phobos-developers/Phobos).
- SyringeEx (LGPL-3.0), which injects DLLs as a debugger.
- cnc-ddraw (MIT, 3.5k stars; GDI, OpenGL and D3D9 renderers, GLSL and libretro shaders, upscaling, and Wine on macOS; https://github.com/FunkyFr3sh/cnc-ddraw).
- ReShade through the D3D9 renderer.
The richest HD work that exists today is the closed Toumao modified ReShade (PNG-sequence animations and game textures). It is bundled in DeathFishAtEase/YRModdingBase (https://github.com/DeathFishAtEase/YRModdingBase, custom non-commercial licence) with Ares 3.0p1, Phobos, KratosPP and FA2SP. The native route is more mature for HD: in-process hooks at native speed, a large community (Mental Omega, CnCNet). But it only runs on Windows (Wine or CrossOver on the M5), it is not a web deliverable, and its most advanced HD piece has an unclear or non-commercial licence. INFERENCE: the VM can reuse the same YRpp address knowledge without DLL injection, by patching guest memory from the host.
risks: LEGAL (high): on every page load, src/main.ts to src/adapter/thirdPartyFiles.ts downloads EA's copyrighted game.exe and gamemd.exe from https://oldgame.store. src/games/downloadCatalog.ts also links full-game downloads on unofficial sites. A public fork should replace this with user-supplied executables (checked by hash, with a clear explanation if the hash does not match) before anything is shared.

IP: RA2/YR, their art and their names belong to EA. Only a non-commercial fan project is realistic, and AI-regenerated HD art is still a derivative of EA assets. EA has released source for other C&C games but not RA2 (HN thread https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45991853).

Maturity: public for about 2 weeks, labelled Alpha, 12 squashed commits, a small team, much of the code written by AI agents, and the real development branch ('dev') is private. The upstream could stall or change direction without notice, and outside PRs go to main only.
Version lock: every hook and patch checks one exact executable hash (RA2 1.006 and YR 1.001). Other builds (Steam, EA App, CD, 1.000) would need new addresses and signatures.

Performance is unmeasured: v86 is a single-core JIT emulator. Game logic plus software blitting of every pixel run in one emulated CPU. Big late-game battles, 1080p or higher resolutions, and extra draw-hook overhead may drop simulation FPS. No published FPS figures exist, and I could not measure without assets.

HD ceiling: today only final-frame post-processing exists. Genuine HD sprites, meshes, water and weather need reverse-engineered hooks per game version (layers L1–L3). That is a large, specialised x86 RE effort, far easier for YR (thanks to YRpp) than for RA2 1.006.

Mixing HD layers with the original frame risks visible seams: z-order and occlusion, team-colour remap, palette tint, shadows, and UI protection all have to be correct. The authors warn that 'enlarging or overlaying images on final frames cannot establish correctness'.
Multiplayer limits: no reconnect or match resume, no authentication, no desync or CRC acceptance, 8-player long matches unverified, and no CnCNet interop.
Ares and Phobos are not supported, so modern community engine features (and mods such as Mental Omega) are unavailable unless someone builds a Syringe-equivalent inside the VM.

GPL-3.0 copyleft: all fork code must stay GPL. Some SR model weights are CC BY-NC-SA and cannot ship. YRpp has no licence file, and the Toumao ReShade plugin is closed with an unclear licence, so neither can be copied in; only addresses and facts can be used.
The brief's premise is wrong: the cited HN item 45991853 is Chrono Divide (a reimplementation), not RA2 VM, so any conclusions drawn from that thread belong to Chrono Divide.
score_rationale:
Step 1 (original game running faithfully on the web) fits this base about 9/10. It runs the real RA2 and YR executables, so rules, AI, units, superweapons and campaigns are the originals by construction. Save/load, FMV, music and EVA, LAN multiplayer over a relay, custom maps and INI/MIX mods already work. The build is clean (918 tests pass on this Mac), and the engineering discipline is unusually high: hash- and signature-checked patches, explicit ownership rules, and good docs. It is GPL-3.0, so we can fork it legally.

Step 2 (a 2026-level 2.5D HD remaster) fits about 4–5/10. The current pipeline only sees the final RGB565 frame. Upscalers and post-FX are ready for quick visible gains, but real HD assets, modern water, weather, impacts and voxel-to-mesh need new hooks into guest code and reads of guest memory (Z-buffer, water and shroud masks, captured draw calls). In the extreme case that means a new host-side renderer fed by game state. This is feasible, and YRpp addresses for YR 1.001 help a lot, but it is a large reverse-engineering effort with unmeasured CPU-emulation headroom, and it is much harder for the RA2 1.006 exe.

Deductions: legal exposure from the automatic exe download, a 2-week-old Alpha upstream with a private dev branch, and no Ares/Phobos. I give 7/10 overall. It is the best choice if faithfulness and 'not from scratch' matter most and we accept a phased HD plan: post-FX, then helper buffers, then selective HD sprites, then a host renderer. A reimplementation with its own scene-graph renderer would score higher on the HD ceiling but lower on fidelity.
